name: Kids wear, toys and baby stores
shape_facts: Mix of categories: clothing, toys, baby essentials (diapers, formula, feeding), gear (prams, car seats, cots), school items.
Number of stores and online channels (website, Instagram, Daraz, Noon, Amazon, FirstCry-style marketplaces).
Own label clothing vs imported brands vs local wholesale.
Whether consumables with expiry (formula, baby food, wipes, diapers) are sold.
Import share and countries of origin for toys and gear.
Whether gift wrapping, birthday hampers or registries are offered.
Whether school uniforms are supplied under arrangements with schools.
scope_rule: pi notes the operational problems: age-size stock, expiry of consumables, gift and seasonal peaks, imports, online orders, returns, staff and reporting. pi gives no child health, infant feeding, product safety certification, toy-safety standard, car-seat installation, or customs advice. pi never collects children’s names, ages linked to identities, birthdays, photos, or parents’ details; it records categories and counts. Any report of a product injuring a child is treated as urgent: pi points to medical help and emergency services, and notes the recall/complaint handling as an operational issue only.

vocabulary.gear: prams, strollers, car seats, cots, high chairs
vocabulary.hamper: gift basket for births or birthdays
vocabulary.registry: list of items parents want as gifts
vocabulary.recall: manufacturer’s request to return an unsafe product
vocabulary.uniform contract: arrangement to supply a school’s uniforms
vocabulary.import consignment: shipment of imported toys or gear

problems.phrase: Kids outgrow sizes so fast that our age-size stock never matches demand
Formula and baby food nearing expiry, we only notice when a mother complains
Diaper prices change every month and our shelf prices lag
Toy imports stuck at customs before Eid or Christmas
Big gear like prams sits for months and blocks space
Toys with missing parts or broken in the box get returned
Battery toys stop working within a week, customers want refunds
We had a supplier recall and couldn’t find who bought the item
Gift buyers want exchanges and we have no proper policy
Parents ask on WhatsApp if we have a size and we reply hours later
Birthday hamper orders get mixed up or delivered late
Online orders of bulky items cost us a fortune to deliver
Daraz/Noon listings out of stock while we have it in store
Same toy is cheaper online than in our shop
Mothers buy once and never come back
No idea who our repeat buyers are for diapers and formula
Ad spend for the Eid toys sale didn’t seem to bring footfall
School uniform orders come all in two weeks and we can’t stitch fast enough
School pays for uniforms late
Kids open and damage toys in store
Small toys and accessories disappear
Staff can’t explain features of prams and car seats
We don’t know margin by category: toys vs clothing vs consumables
Dollar/dirham rate changes make imported toys expensive overnight
Christmas/Eid toy buying is a guess every year
Inventory is in Excel with thousands of small SKUs

stock: Which ages or sizes run out most?
Which categories sit on shelves longest?
consumables: Do you sell formula, baby food or diapers?
How do you keep an eye on expiry dates?
imports: Where do your toys and gear come from?
How often do shipments arrive late for a season?
quality: How do you handle a supplier recall today?
customers: Do you know your regular buyers of consumables?
How do parents usually contact you?
online: What’s the hardest part of delivering bulky items?
school: What’s the toughest part of the uniform rush?
margin: Which category do you think makes the most money?
How do currency changes affect your import prices?
planning: How do you decide what to buy for Eid or the holidays?

seasons: Pakistan: Eid ul-Fitr (kids’ clothes and toys peak, Eidi spending), Eid ul-Adha, back-to-school and uniforms (March– April and August), winter kids’ wear Nov–Jan, birthday-party demand year-round, summer holidays June–August for toys. UAE: Ramadan and Eid, back-to-school (late August and term changes), Dubai Shopping Festival, Christmas for expat families, summer camps and travel gear before summer. Canada: Christmas (largest toy peak), Black Friday/Boxing Day, back-to-school, Halloween costumes, winter outerwear Oct–Dec, Eid and Diwali for diaspora stores.
care: Any child injury, choking or allergic reaction linked to a product: pi first points to emergency or medical help, then notes only the operational follow-up.
Infant feeding, formula choice or medical claims: out of scope; pi gives no advice.
Toy and car-seat safety standards and certifications: noted as admin/compliance effort, no advice.
Selling recalled, expired or counterfeit products: pi declines to help.
Children’s and parents’ personal data, photos for marketing: not collected; pi does not help use child photos without consent.
Customs on toy imports: no advice; under-declaration declined.
Infant-formula pricing rules or restrictions where they apply: noted, no legal guidance.
build_ideas: Age-size stock grid for clothing across stores and online, with sell-through by age band.
Expiry and batch register for consumables, with alerts and a near-expiry action list.
Batch/serial capture for gear and electronic toys so recall lookups can find which sales are affected.
Price update workflow for consumables when supplier prices change.
Repeat-purchase reminders on WhatsApp for consumables (opt-in), based on purchase intervals.
WhatsApp stock-check flow: parent asks for an item/size, staff reply from a live stock lookup.
Hamper and birthday order tracker with event date, contents, delivery slot and status.
Import shipment tracker by consignment with expected arrival vs season deadline.
Returns and defect log by product and supplier with claim status.
Category margin dashboard (clothing, toys, consumables, gear) including currency-adjusted landed cost.
School uniform order board: sizes per class, production status, delivery and invoice tracking.
Marketplace stock sync for Daraz, Noon or Amazon.
Seasonal buying planner using last year’s Eid/Christmas sales by category.

exchange.text: We sell formula and baby food, and last week a customer found an expired tin on the shelf. Very embarrassing.
That’s a stressful one, I’m sorry — noted, expired formula reached the shelf and a customer found it. Right now, how does the team keep track of expiry dates?
Someone is supposed to check monthly but it doesn’t really happen.
Got it, noted — the monthly expiry check isn’t happening reliably. Roughly how many baby food and formula items do you carry?
Thanks, I’ve added that. Do expiry dates get written down anywhere when stock arrives?
